Server mode accepts incoming connections and can discard or actively send data.
Supports unlimited or bandwidth-controlled traffic.
Supports TCP and RFC6455 WebSocket transport.
Supports TLS/SSL connections.
Can measure TCP connect latency, time to first byte, and request-response latency.
Supports message markers for message-rate and message-arrival-latency measurements.
Supports multi-threaded operation and very high connection counts.
tcpkali.pricing: Free and open source; BSD-2-Clause license. No paid pricing was found.

testable-io.about: Testable is a cloud or self-managed platform for functional, API, performance, and load testing. Its load-testing product distributes tests across scalable runners, supports Testable infrastructure or customer infrastructure, and can run Selenium, Puppeteer, and Playwright tests as load tests.
features: Scalable distributed load and performance testing
Execution on Testable cloud infrastructure, customer infrastructure, or self-hosted runners
Support for Selenium, Puppeteer, Playwright, JMeter, Gatling, Locust, Node.js, and WebSocket testing
Test execution from more than 100 regions across AWS, Azure, and Google Cloud
Real-time collection and aggregation of metrics, traces, assertions, logs, screenshots, and videos
Intelligent multimedia sampling and detailed request traces
Configurable success criteria and CI/CD automation through API, scheduling, and integrations
Execution-results APIs for metrics, logs, traces, reports, and downloadable result files
testable-io.pricing: Testable offers a free Monitoring plan with up to 50 configured monitors; pricing for testing plans is plan-based. The official pricing page lists Team at $99/month promotional pricing ($149/month listed comparison price), Pro at $399/month promotional pricing ($599/month listed comparison price), and Automation plans with displayed prices including $99/month and $129/month. Exact load-testing costs and usage limits are not clearly identified in the retrieved pricing excerpt.
aiFeatures: AI Scenario: natural-language instructions generate and execute a Playwright browser-automation script.
AI Conversations: an agent workspace can create, update, run, investigate, summarize, and analyze testing resources.
AI-assisted setup can generate scripts from plain-language steps; generated scripts may be cached and reused for later deterministic runs.

the-grinder.about: The Grinder is a freely available, BSD-style open-source Java load-testing framework for running distributed tests across multiple load-injector machines. It uses worker processes, agent processes, and a console.
features: Distributed load testing across multiple machines
Worker, agent, and console process architecture
Test scripting with Jython, Java, or Clojure support
Mature HTTP plug-in with client-connection and cookie management
HTTP script recording and replay through the TCP Proxy
Support for testing custom protocols through Java code
Console-based control plus statistics, reports, and charts
the-grinder.pricing: Free; the official manual describes The Grinder as freely available under a BSD-style open-source license.
the-grinder.authorOrCompany: The Grinder project; the supplied repository is maintained under the cossme/grinder GitHub organization, with releases attributed to solcyr.

latestRelease.notes: The Grinder 4.0.0 provides a new web-based graphical console. The associated release-preparation commit is dated 2018-03-11.

tsung.about: Tsung is an open-source, distributed, multi-protocol load-testing and high-performance benchmarking tool for testing the scalability and performance of IP-based client/server applications.
features: Distributed load generation across client machines
High-performance simulation of thousands of users on a single CPU
Protocol plug-ins for HTTP, WebDAV, SOAP, PostgreSQL, MySQL, LDAP, MQTT, AMQP, and Jabber/XMPP
SSL support
HTTP proxy mode for recording sessions
XML-defined user behavior and scenarios
Real-time statistics, customizable transactions, and generated graphical reports
Operating-system monitoring of CPU, memory, and network traffic via Erlang agents or SNMP
tsung.pricing: Free and open source under the GNU General Public License v2.0. The project also documents optional commercial support/professional services, but no product pricing is listed.
tsung.authorOrCompany: Tsung community; maintained in the processone/tsung GitHub repository.

vegeta.about: Vegeta is a versatile HTTP load-testing tool designed to exercise HTTP services at a constant request rate. It is available as both a command-line utility and a Go library.
features: Command-line tool and Go library
UNIX-composable CLI
Avoids Coordinated Omission
Extensive reporting functionality
Support for distributed load testing
Easy installation and execution via static binaries and package managers

visual-studio-load-test.about: Visual Studio Load Test was Microsoft's web performance and load-testing functionality for simulating many users accessing a server concurrently. Its cloud-based load-testing service and the Visual Studio functionality have been deprecated/end-of-lifed; Visual Studio 2019 was the last version with full web performance and load-test capability, while limited support for running existing tests remained in Visual Studio 2022.
features: Web performance tests
Load tests for web or unit tests
Cloud execution across multiple virtual machines/agents (deprecated)
On-premises execution using Test Controller and Test Agent
Web-based load-test experience supporting URL-based tests, HAR files, Apache JMeter, and Visual Studio web tests
CI/CD load-testing tasks through Azure DevOps (deprecated)
Test recording/web recorder support, dependent on Internet Explorer and itself deprecated

latestRelease.version: Visual Studio 2019 (last version with full web performance and load-test functionality)
latestRelease.notes: Microsoft announced that Visual Studio 2019 would be the last version with web performance and load-test features. The Azure DevOps cloud-based load-testing service continued through March 31, 2020; cloud-based load testing for Visual Studio was no longer supported after that date. Microsoft documentation states that Visual Studio 2022 can run existing web/load tests, but templates for creating new tests were removed, and recommends Azure Load Testing as an alternative.

wapt-pro.about: WAPT Pro is SoftLogica’s scalable web-application performance/load-testing tool for creating and running distributed tests locally, remotely, or in cloud environments, supporting up to 1 million concurrent users.
features: Browser- and mobile-application session recording
Distributed testing with multiple load agents and cloud support
Support for AJAX/RIA and major web technologies
Server and database monitoring via SNMP, WMI, ODBC, and Apache interfaces
Flexible error handling, customizable pass/fail criteria, and result-analysis functions
Runtime charts and customizable reports with more than 20 tables
Embedded JavaScript for in-session calculations
CSV export of raw timing data
wapt-pro.pricing: The official pricing pages show WAPT Pro license prices varying by purchase/upgrade option. The current order page lists WAPT Pro pricing components including $750 or $1,000 for the product in one pricing table, with additional load-agent licensing available; an official quick-start PDF lists an initial license price of $1,200 USD plus a $300 annual subscription fee. WAPT Pro includes two load agents; demo versions are limited to 20 concurrent virtual users.

webload.about: WebLOAD is RadView’s performance, scalability, and reliability/load-testing solution for Internet applications. It generates virtual-client traffic to test applications under load and provides performance statistics and reporting.

Virtual-client simulation and probing clients for targeted activity measurements
HTTP/HTTPS and WebSocket protocol support
Automatic recording and support for AJAX, XML, JSON, and binary data
Correlation and parameterization for dynamic/session-specific values
JavaScript scripting with Java access and extensive scripting functions
Real-time graphical/statistical reporting, analytics, and browser-based dashboards
Cloud load generation and scalable execution

weighttp.about: weighttp is a lightweight, simple webserver benchmarking tool from the lighttpd project. It is designed to be fast and lean, supporting only a small subset of HTTP/1.x.
features: Multithreading for use of multiple CPU cores
Event-driven I/O for concurrent requests within one thread

HTTP benchmarking with configurable request count, threads, concurrency, keep-alive, pipelining, IPv6, HTTP methods, headers, cookies, authentication, proxy support, TCP Fast Open, and POST/PUT content types
CSV output of response-time percentiles
Build support via Autotools and Meson
weighttp.pricing: Free and open source under the MIT License; no commercial pricing is documented in the retrieved official sources.

wrk.about: wrk is a modern HTTP benchmarking tool that generates significant load from a single multi-core CPU using a multithreaded design and scalable event notification systems such as epoll and kqueue.
features: Multithreaded HTTP benchmarking
Scalable event notification via epoll and kqueue
Optional LuaJIT scripting for HTTP request generation, response processing, and custom reporting
Latency and request statistics
HTTP pipelining
TLS support, including hostname transmission via TLS SNI
Configurable threads, connections, duration, timeout, rate, and script options
wrk.pricing: Free and open source; the repository is licensed under a modified Apache 2.0 license. No paid pricing is documented for wg/wrk.

wrk2.about: wrk2 is an HTTP benchmarking tool based mostly on wrk. It modifies wrk to generate constant-throughput load and provide accurate high-percentile latency measurements, including handling of Coordinated Omission.
features: Constant-throughput load generation via --rate or -R, measured in total requests per second.
Accurate high-percentile latency recording, including 99.9999th-percentile results when run long enough.
Multithreaded HTTP benchmarking using scalable event notification systems such as epoll and kqueue.
Optional LuaJIT scripting for HTTP request generation, response processing, and custom reporting.
Supports wrk-style HTTP benchmarking arguments and statistics output.
wrk2.pricing: Free and open source under the Apache License 2.0; no commercial pricing is documented.

xlt.about: XLT (Xceptance LoadTest) is an open-source, Java/JVM-based regression, load, performance, and test-automation tool. It supports load testing as code, WebDriver-style browser automation, scalable distributed execution, real-time monitoring, and detailed reports.
features: Java-based scripting and execution on platforms with a supported JDK
Load testing as code using Java, with IDE/JUnit and Maven or Gradle integration
WebDriver-style real-browser automation and client-side performance testing
Distributed, highly scalable execution across machines, locations, and cloud infrastructure
Ready-to-use, customizable single-run, comparison, and trend reports
Real-time test monitoring and result browsing/diagnostics
Open-format result data and HTML reports
Jenkins integration for continuous load testing and automated result evaluation
xlt.pricing: Free and open source under the Apache License 2.0. Xceptance separately offers XTC, a hosted cloud version of XLT, with pricing not established here.

Supports multiple request/ammo formats, including URL lists, access logs, and request-style formats

Standard workloads with configurable properties and operations
Load and run benchmark workloads through ycsb command-line scripts
Bindings for systems including Accumulo, Cassandra, Couchbase, DynamoDB, Elasticsearch, HBase, JDBC, MongoDB, Redis, and Tarantool
